title: gantry.json
description: Configuration for a Gantry desktop app - read by the gantry CLI (dev, build, gen).

$schema.description: Reference to this schema, enabling editor validation and hover docs.

name.description: The app's identity: exe name, Go module name, WebView2 data folder and log namespace. Lowercase, path-safe.

title.description: Human-facing name: the window title, tray tooltip and installer display name.

version.description: App version, shown by installers (Setup.exe's AppVersion).

gantry.description: The Gantry framework version this app was scaffolded with or last brought to by gantry upgrade. Maintained by the CLI.

port.description: Local server port the app binds on 127.0.0.1 - also the single-instance guard. The dev proxy forwards /api and /gantry/ws here.

mode.description: Informational: whether the app was scaffolded single-page (pages/index only) or multi-page. Adding page folders is what actually changes routing.

style.description: Informational: the page style the scaffold generated - Tea (UI logic in Go) or plain React with paired handlers.

tailwind.description: Adds the @tailwindcss/vite plugin to the synthesized Vite config. Set by gantry new --tailwind or gantry install --tailwind; the tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/vite packages must be in package.json.

tray.description: Informational: whether the scaffold wired a system tray. The live switch is gantry.Config.Tray in main.go, and any built app can be launched with --tray or --no-tray.

buttons.description: Informational: which window buttons the scaffold enabled. The live switches are the WindowOptions fields in main.go.

minimize.description: Whether the scaffold enabled the minimize button.

maximize.description: Whether the scaffold enabled the maximize button.

close.description: Whether the scaffold enabled the close button.

icons.description: Directory (relative to the app root) holding the default icon files: icon.ico (Windows exe + tray) and icon.png (window, Linux tray). gantry build bakes icon.ico into the exe; gantry gen embeds both as runtime defaults. Code-level Icon settings override them.

args.description: Custom app arguments, keyed by flag name (lowercase-kebab). gantry dev validates them on its command line (gantry dev --api-host=10.0.0.5) and passes each to the app as an environment variable: the explicit "env" name, or GANTRY_ARG_<UPPER_SNAKE> derived from the flag name. A production binary reads the same variables at launch, falling back to the declared default - so a shipped exe needs nothing set. Read them with gantry.Arg/ArgBool/ArgInt in Go and useEnv()/useArg() in React.

type.description: The arg's type. Bool flags are passed as --name or --name=false (stdlib flag syntax); string and int take --name=value or --name value.

default.description: Value when the flag/env var is absent. Must match the declared type. Defaults to the type's zero value ("", false, 0).

description.description: One-line help shown by gantry dev --help.

env.description: Explicit environment variable name; defaults to GANTRY_ARG_<UPPER_SNAKE> derived from the flag name (api-host -> GANTRY_ARG_API_HOST).

targets.description: Build targets as os/arch pairs. Empty or absent = the current machine only. Windows and mac targets cross-compile from anywhere; linux targets need a Linux machine (WSL works). android (bare = arm64) builds an APK when the JDK/SDK/NDK toolchain is present, and is skipped with a warning otherwise; ios is an experimental scaffold.

console.description: Keep the console window on Windows builds (debug builds; release builds are windowed apps).

installer.description: Also produce install artifacts per target: a Setup.exe via Inno Setup on Windows (the .iss is left ready when Inno Setup is not installed), a .tar.gz on Linux, a .zip on Mac.

mobile.description: Mobile settings, needed by the android and ios build targets: app identity, friendly permissions, home-screen widgets and per-OS options.

id.description: Application id in reverse-DNS form (Android applicationId / iOS bundle id base), e.g. ec.morrison.demo. Changing it after release makes stores treat the app as a different app.

permissions.description: Friendly permission names, mapped to the platform's real permissions at build time (Android manifest entries now, iOS usage strings later). INTERNET is always included - the app talks to its own local server.

widgets.description: Android home-screen widgets. Each entry must have a paired widgets/<name>/<name>.go exporting its Widget; the entry holds launcher metadata only.

label.description: Name shown in the launcher's widget picker. Defaults to the widget name.

minSize.description: Minimum size in launcher grid cells as CxR, e.g. 3x1.

maxSize.description: Maximum size in launcher grid cells as CxR.

resize.description: Which axes the user can resize the widget on.

refreshMinutes.description: Background refresh period in minutes (Android floors periodic work at 15).

keystore.description: Release signing key. Absent = the APK is signed with a debug key (installable, not store-ready).

file.description: Path to the .jks/.keystore file, relative to the app root.

passwordEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the keystore/key password - the password itself never goes in gantry.json.

bundleId.description: Bundle identifier override; defaults to mobile.id.
